digest.en: COP31 closed in Brazil without a new climate pact, leaving the global framework intact but fragile. Meanwhile, Iran is rationing electricity as its power grid buckles under the strain of recent US and Israeli strikes. The diplomatic silence in Geneva contrasts sharply with the operational reality in Tehran.
digest.hi: नेतन्याहू और आइजनकोट की चार घंटे की बैठक ने इज़राइल की अगली सरकार के रूप तय करने का काम शुरू कर दिया है। इसी समय कनाडा में गोद भराई समारोह के दौरान हुई गोलीबारी में तीन लोगों की मौत हो गई। यूरोप में बच्चों के लिए एआई पर रोक की बहस भी तेज हो रही है।

articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
articles.summary: Gadi Eisenkot labeled recent West Bank arson by Jewish settlers as Jewish terrorism. He argued these extremist acts undermine regional stability and endanger lives. The former defense minister warned the attacks damage Israel's national security and foreign relations. Gadi Eisenkot called the attacks ‘Jewish terrorism’, saying that ‘extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations’.

articles.title: A weak South China Sea code of conduct will be worse than no agreement at all
articles.summary: Collin Koh argues a weak South China Sea code of conduct is worse than no agreement. Singapore will chair ASEAN in 2027. The remaining unresolved issues are the most intractable. Koh believes a flawed deal creates more problems than silence. As Singapore takes over as ASEAN chair in 2027, what remains unresolved on the South China Sea code of conduct are arguably the most intractable issues, says Collin Koh from the S Rajaratnam School of International Studies.

articles.title: India's space startups are going global. Why is that sparking debate at home?
articles.summary: A satellite startup's US defense expansion sparked domestic debate in India. Questions arose about whether international operations influence government projects. Experts discussed balancing overseas growth with national interests. The industry views global expansion as essential for long-term viability. A satellite startup's US defence expansion has prompted questions over whether its international operations could influence Indian government projects. Experts tell CNA why overseas business matters to the industry and how companies can balance growth with national interests.

articles.title: Rescuers Search For Victims After Russia Attacks Apartment Building Near Kyiv
articles.summary: Russian drones destroyed a residential building in Dymer, 45 kilometers north of Kyiv. At least five people died, including an 18-year-old man. Rescuers searched for survivors and other victims. The attack targeted a civilian area near the capital. At least five people were confirmed dead after Russian drone strikes destroyed a residential building in the town of Dymer, about 45 kilometers north of Kyiv.

articles.title: South Korean minister quits after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
articles.summary: South Korea's education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday following an AI cheating scandal. He admitted failing to prepare adequately for university entrance exams. The tests banned phones and checked for hidden cameras. The resignation follows widespread fears over AI-assisted fraud in the country's key academic assessments. Choi Kyo-jin said he ‘failed to prepare adequately’ for entrance exams, which this year had phones banned and checks for cameras hidden in clothingSouth Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted in the lead-up to the country’s key university entrance exams. articles.title: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief warns there is ‘no ambiguity in the science’
articles.summary: COP31 concluded without a binding climate agreement. Negotiators failed to resolve disputes over fossil fuel phaseouts. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the outcome deeply disappointing. The two-week summit ended with no new commitments to accelerate global emissions reductions. COP31 ended on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to overcome divisions over fossil fuels, bringing two weeks of talks and two days of overtime to a close that UN Secretary-General António Guterres described as a “deeply disappointing” setback.

articles.title: ‘I had a better life in Iran’: Afghan women forced home struggle to rebuild
articles.summary: Afghan women returning from Iran face unemployment and fractured families. Zahra, a midwife in Herat, lost her income and now lives with her parents. Her son remains with her ex-husband. The five-year displacement left her without a stable livelihood or support network in her home region. For five years, Zahra cared for an elderly woman in Iran and earned enough to get by.

articles.title: Afghan Women Turn To Social Media To Earn Living As Doors Close Offline
articles.summary: Afghan women are building personal brands on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube to earn income. They share videos of cooking, shopping, and family gatherings. This digital shift offers a livelihood as offline opportunities have closed under Taliban restrictions. Afghan women who have had their lives sharply restricted by Taliban rule have responded by building personal brands on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube showing them cooking at home, shopping in bazaars, or meeting friends and family.

articles.title: China’s open-weight AI models are coming for America’s market
articles.summary: The Trump administration is considering requiring US companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. This move follows growing adoption of tools from DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Moonshot AI. American firms are shifting to these lower-cost alternatives. The deliberation aims to address the rising market share of Chinese open-weight models in the United States. The Trump administration is weighing whether to require American companies to disclose their use of Chinese artificial intelligence, Reuters reported on November 18.

articles.title: Iran To Ration Electricity Amid Warnings Power Grid Battered by US, Israeli Strikes
articles.summary: Iran will begin rationing electricity on November 22. This follows recent bread shortages and purchase management procedures. The move occurs as uncertainty grows over President Trump’s next diplomatic or military step. The government aims to manage domestic resource scarcity. Iran To Ration Electricity As World Awaits Trump's Next Move. Iran To Ration Electricity Amid Warnings Power Grid Battered by US, Israeli Strikes.

articles.title: ‘We escaped with only our lives’: Fighting to give birth in war-torn Yemen
articles.summary: Midwife Anisa Fadhl fled Taiz, Yemen, as fighting escalated two months ago. She left without packing a bag. Her home and clinic were later looted and destroyed. She escaped with only her life. The conflict displaced many medical workers. When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz, in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl had no time to pack a bag before she fled, leaving behind her home and her clinic.

articles.title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
articles.summary: El Salvador deployed troops to Port-au-Prince to combat gangs, drawing mixed reactions from Haitians. Many welcomed the intervention after years of gang control, but others fear the offensive will worsen the volatile security situation in the capital. Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situationA bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground.

articles.title: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve
articles.summary: China pledged to accelerate low-carbon electrification and assist other nations in doing the same. Wang Yi made the commitment at the Cop31 summit. The goal aligns with broader calls for countries to derive 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035. Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy.

articles.title: Why Takaichi should stick to her guns on Taiwan
articles.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated Chinese force against Taiwan could trigger Self-Defense Forces deployment. The remark drew significant criticism from Beijing. China responded with economic and diplomatic pressure against Tokyo. On November 7, 2025, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was pressed repeatedly in parliament about a possible Chinese invasion or naval blockade of Taiwan. She eventually said that Chinese use of force could trigger the deployment of Japan’s Self-Defense Forces.

articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
articles.summary: Donald Trump threatened to impose severe penalties on American tech firms constructing datacenters outside the United States. He made the statement during a White House press conference on Friday. The president provided no specific details regarding the nature or scale of these penalties. He also admitted he had not yet briefed his own officials on the plan. articles.title: Pontoon Bridges, Hydrofoils, Tunnels: Barraged By Russia, Kyiv Rushes For Alternative River
articles.summary: Russia is targeting bridges spanning the Dnieper River in Kyiv. Ukrainian officials are developing alternatives to keep the city connected. Plans include pontoon bridges, hydrofoils, and tunnels. The goal is to prevent the capital from being cut in half. Russia is deliberately targeting the vital bridges that span the Dnieper River -- and link the two sides of Kyiv. Ukrainian officials are scrambling to come up with alternatives in case the city is completely cut in half.

articles.title: With Oil Revenue Running Out, Iran Teases Breaking US Blockade
articles.summary: Iranian hardliners are pushing for a tanker convoy to break the US naval blockade as oil revenue hits zero by mid-December. They threaten to strike Persian Gulf oil sites if the US fires on the vessels. This escalation risks a direct military confrontation in the region. With Iran’s oil revenue set to hit zero by mid-December, IRGC-linked media and hard-liners are pushing for a tanker convoy to break through the US naval blockade, threatening Persian Gulf oil sites if fired on.

articles.title: Countries demand stronger climate deal amid deadlock in Antalya
articles.summary: A coalition of countries challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit fossil fuel action. They also called for stronger climate finance commitments. Tensions rose as the Antalya summit neared its close. Negotiators struggled to find a deal acceptable to nearly 200 governments. A group of countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific has challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit action on fossil fuels and stronger climate finance.

articles.title: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers
articles.summary: Israeli settlers carried out over 400 attacks during this year’s West Bank olive harvest. This is the highest number recorded in any previous season. UN agencies and humanitarian groups urged Israel to protect farmers from the violence. The attacks caused casualties and significant property damage. Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank – more than in any previous season, UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said on Friday.

articles.title: Shattered playgrounds and freezing classrooms: Inside Ukraine’s deadliest year for children
articles.summary: UNICEF highlighted record child casualty levels in Ukraine as the country faces another brutal winter. A twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten stands in ruins during a day-long power cut. Freezing classrooms and shattered playgrounds illustrate the dangers children face. The conflict continues to inflict severe harm on the youngest population. Amid the ruins of a twice-bombed Kyiv kindergarten as a day-long power cut continued, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) on Friday highlighted the dangers to youngsters enduring another brutal winter in Ukraine, as child casualty numbers rise to record levels.

articles.title: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
articles.summary: The President of the United Nations General Assembly visited Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh one day after the International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. The visit aimed to pressure the international community to translate the landmark legal finding into concrete protective measures. The court’s decision marks a significant shift in the diplomatic handling of the crisis. The President urged member states to move beyond rhetoric and implement the court’s directives.

articles.title: Bridgetown AI summit to tackle safety as risks outpace capacity to respond
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres co-hosted an AI safety summit in Bridgetown, Barbados. The gathering aimed to close the gap between accelerating technological risks and the limited capacity of many nations to manage the pace of development. UN Secretary-General António Guterres is heading to Barbados to co-host a special summit on artificial intelligence (AI) safety on Monday, aimed at closing the gap between accelerating risks and many countries’ capacity to deal with the pace of development.

articles.title: The secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
articles.summary: Cuban asylum seeker Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez ended a hunger strike in Texas. He described being force-fed through a tube after five days of resistance. The physical pain forced him to stop the protest. articles.title: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
articles.summary: The latest draft climate agreement for COP31 removed explicit language on phasing out fossil fuels. This deletion occurred as ministers and the Presidency attempted to bridge sharp differences before the summit's scheduled close. Civil society groups expressed serious concern over the missing commitment. The change signals a significant retreat in the text's ambition regarding energy transition. A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday.

articles.title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
articles.summary: GPS and radio signals are increasingly blocked or faked, endangering aid convoys, passenger jets, and cargo ships. Civilian safety is declining as these critical navigation systems become unreliable. The disruption affects both conflict zones and open ocean routes. From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions.

articles.summary: तिरुचिरापल्ली में सड़क हादसे में आठ लोगों की मौत हुई। प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने परिजनों के लिए मुआवजे की घोषणा की। दो अन्य घायल हैं। तमिलनाडु के तिरुचिरपापल्ली जिले में रविवार को हुए भीषण हादसे में 8 लोगों की मौत हो गई, जबकि दो लोग गंभीर रूप से घायल हुए हैं. प्रधानमंत्री मोदी ने इस हादसे पर दुख जताया है और मृतकों के परिजनों और घायलों के लिए मुआवजे का ऐलान किया है.

articles.title: H-1B Visa पर सख्ती का असर अमेरिकी नौकरियों पर भी पड़ सकता है? जानिए रिसर्च में क्या हुआ खुलासा
articles.summary: कैटो इंस्टीट्यूट का शोध बताता है कि एच-1बी वीजा पर सख्ती अमेरिकी नागरिकों की नौकरियों को भी प्रभावित कर सकती है। हेज फंड डेटा इस बात का समर्थन करता है। H-1B Visa Restrictions: अमरीका में एच-1बी वीजा को लेकर सख्ती की कोशिशों के बीच एक नए शोध ने इस बहस को नया मोड़ दे दिया है। शोध के अनुसार, विदेशी उच्च कुशल पेशेवरों की नियुक्ति पर पाबंदियां लगाने से केवल प्रवासी कर्मचारियों के अवसर ही प्रभावित नहीं होंगे, बल्कि अमरीकी नागरिकों की नौकरियों पर भी इसका असर पड़ सकता है।

articles.summary: जम्मू-कश्मीर स्टूडेंट्स एसोसिएशन ने अमित शाह से FAA परीक्षा में नकल की जांच के लिए CBI को भेजने की मांग की। संगठन ने स्वतंत्र जांच की वकालत की। जम्मू-कश्मीर स्टूडेंट्स एसोसिएशन (JKSA) ने रविवार को केंद्रीय गृह मंत्री अमित शाह को पत्र लिखकर, फाइनेंस अकाउंट्स असिस्टेंट (FAA) भर्ती परीक्षा के दौरान कथित तौर पर संगठित तरीके से की गई नकल और परीक्षा में हुई गड़बड़ियों में हस्तक्षेप करने की मांग की है.
